plate_findings.evidence: Plain radiographs of the left knee ... shows "worm-like" calcifications in the soft tissues caused by dead calcified worms

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Real human plain radiograph of the left knee from a patient with dracunculiasis; caption explicitly attributes the arrow-marked serpentine soft-tissue calcifications to dead calcified Guinea worms, matching the classic radiographic presentation of calcified worm tracks. b: Real human plain radiograph of the left leg of the same dracunculiasis patient; the arrow indicates a linear serpentine soft-tissue calcification identified in the caption as a dead calcified worm, the classic radiographic finding of dracunculiasis. c: Axial CT slices of the left leg of the same human patient; arrows point to small calcified foci in the subcutaneous tissue and musculature that the caption confirms as dead calcified Guinea worms, consistent with the classic calcified worm track presentation of dracunculiasis on cross-sectional imaging.
panels.attribution_text: Rodríguez Carnero et al. Unexpected hosts: imaging parasitic diseases.. Insights into imaging 2017. doi:10.1007/s13244-016-0525-2. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 16.
panels.figure_caption: Dracunculiasis. a and b Plain radiographs of the left knee and leg of a patient coming from Mali shows “worm-like” calcifications in the soft tissues caused by dead calcified worms. c. CT image of the left leg of the same patient as in a and b, confirms the dead calcified worms in the subcutaneous tissue and muscles of the left lower limb

panels.rationale: Single gross image of patient excised subcutaneous tissue from right hip with caption explicitly stating calcified guinea worms in circled areas, in article titled Guinea Worm Disease Presenting as a Subcutaneous Calcification. Real patient specimen showing specific dracunculiasis manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Athavale et al. Guinea Worm Disease Presenting as a Subcutaneous Calcification.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.62733. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Circled areas in excised specimen showing calcified guinea worms
in_text_mentions: On ultrasonography (USG), the subcutaneous foreign body of calcifications was noted in the subcutaneous plane in the right hip region. Soft tissue appeared normal, there was no evidence of fluid in tissue or tendons or soft tissue oedema. After obtaining the consent of the patient, excision and excision of multiple subcutaneous calcifications was planned under spinal anaesthesia and the excised specimen was sent for histopathology examination for definitive diagnosis (Figure 3).
